issue.title: [rsyslog] Read hostname from CONFIG_DB directly; drop shell-built `-a` JSON in rsyslog-config.sh

failure.body:
## Background

`files/image_config/rsyslog/rsyslog.conf.j2` renders the device hostname into three `$template SONiC*` directives (lines 60/62/63) using a Jinja variable `{{ hostname }}` that comes from `-a` in `files/image_config/rsyslog/rsyslog-config.sh`:

```bash
hostname=$(hostname)
...
sonic-cfggen -d -t /usr/share/sonic/templates/rsyslog.conf.j2 \
    -a "{\"udp_server_ip\": \"$udp_server_ip\", \"hostname\": \"$hostname\", \"docker0_ip\": \"$docker0_ip\", \"forward_with_osversion\": \"$syslog_with_osversion\", \"os_version\": \"$os_version\", \"syslog_counter\": \"$syslog_counter\"}" \
    > "$TMPFILE"
```

Every other hostname-consuming template in the tree reads it directly from CONFIG_DB:

- `dockers/docker-fpm-gobgp/zebra.conf.j2:10` — `hostname {{ DEVICE_METADATA['localhost']['hostname'] }}`
- `dockers/docker-fpm-frr/frr/common/daemons.common.conf.j2:4` — same pattern
- `dockers/docker-lldp/lldpd.conf.j2:29` — same pattern (with `\n`/`\r` scrub added in #29264)
- `files/build_templates/qos_config.j2:33` — `{% set hostname = DEVICE_METADATA['localhost']['hostname'] %}`

rsyslog is the only outlier.

## Why change it

1. **Bypasses YANG validation added in #29264.** `$(hostname)` returns the kernel value set by `sethostname(2)`, which accepts any bytes except NUL. Reading `DEVICE_METADATA['localhost']['hostname']` via `sonic-cfggen -d` runs through the same source lldpd uses and benefits from the leaf-level pattern constraint added by #29264.

2. **Removes a fragile hand-quoted JSON blob.** The `-a "{...}"` string interpolates six shell variables into JSON with no escaping. Any embedded `"` or `\` in any of `hostname`, `udp_server_ip`, `docker0_ip`, `syslog_with_osversion`, `os_version`, `syslog_counter` produces malformed JSON. Today only `hostname` and `os_version` are addressed by #29519's sink-side scrub — the other four are latent injection surfaces if their upstream sources ever get looser.

3. **Consistency.** Match the pattern the other four templates already use.

## Proposed change

`files/image_config/rsyslog/rsyslog.conf.j2`:

```diff
-{% set hostname = hostname | replace('\n', '') | replace('\r', '') | replace('"', '') | replace('\\', '') | replace('%', '') -%}
-{% set os_version = os_version | replace('\n', '') | replace('\r', '') | replace('"', '') | replace('\\', '') | replace('%', '') -%}
+{% set hostname = DEVICE_METADATA['localhost']['hostname'] | replace('\n', '') | replace('\r', '') | replace('"', '') | replace('\\', '') | replace('%', '') -%}
+{% set os_version = os_version | replace('\n', '') | replace('\r', '') | replace('"', '') | replace('\\', '') | replace('%', '') -%}
```

`files/image_config/rsyslog/rsyslog-config.sh`:

- Drop `hostname` from the `-a` JSON.
- Keep `os_version` for now (comes from `sonic_version.yml`, not CONFIG_DB — separate follow-up to expose it via `-y` or a metadata table).
- Longer-term: switch the whole `-a` blob to `jq -n --arg ... '{...}'` to remove the quoting hazard for the remaining fields.

Keep the Jinja scrub. Direct `redis-cli hset` writes bypass YANG, so sink-side defense in depth still matters.

Guard against missing `DEVICE_METADATA.hostname` with a Jinja `| default(...)`. Either fall back to `'sonic'` (matches SONiC bootstrap default) or keep `$(hostname)` in `-a` as the fallback and let the template prefer CONFIG_DB when present. Both preserve current behavior in the DEVICE_METADATA-missing edge case; the second option adds no new failure mode vs. today.

## DB availability

`rsyslog-config.service` already has `Requires=config-setup.service` / `After=config-setup.service`, and `rsyslog-config.sh:3` already calls `sonic-db-cli CONFIG_DB HGET 'DEVICE_METADATA|localhost' platform`. If Redis is down, the script already fails today. Switching the hostname source to CONFIG_DB adds no new failure mode.

## Non-goals

- Not a fix for any exploitable vuln — #29519 already closes the rsyslog hostname sink at the Jinja layer.
- Not touching the shared `stypes:hostname` typedef. #29264 chose the leaf-scoped pattern deliberately.

## Verification

- `pytest src/sonic-config-engine/tests/test_j2files.py -k rsyslog` — existing hostname-injection tests should still pass with `additional_data` replaced by a `config_db.json` fragment containing `DEVICE_METADATA.localhost.hostname`.
- Manual: set `DEVICE_METADATA|localhost hostname` to a clean value, run `rsyslog-config.sh`, diff `/etc/rsyslog.conf` — no functional change.

## Related

- #29519 — sink-side scrub for hostname/os_version (this issue is the follow-up cleanup)
- #29264 — YANG leaf pattern on `DEVICE_METADATA.localhost.hostname` + lldpd sink scrub
- Commit 8979ec0f9 — SYSLOG_SERVER field sanitization

resolution.title: [rsyslog]: Read hostname from CONFIG_DB
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it

rsyslog was the only hostname-consuming template sourcing the kernel hostname through hand-built `-a` JSON. Align it with CONFIG_DB-backed templates while retaining sink-side sanitization.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

- **Hostname source**
  - Read `DEVICE_METADATA.localhost.hostname` in `rsyslog.conf.j2`.
  - Fall back to `sonic` when metadata is absent.
  - Retain newline, quote, backslash, and percent-character scrubbing.

```jinja2
{% set hostname = ((DEVICE_METADATA | default({})).get('localhost', {})).get('hostname') | default('sonic', true) | replace('\n', '') | replace('\r', '') | replace('"', '') | replace('\\', '') | replace('%', '') -%}
```

- **cfggen input**
  - Remove `$(hostname)` and the `hostname` field from `rsyslog-config.sh`’s `-a` JSON.
  - Preserve `os_version` and existing runtime inputs.

- **Coverage**
  - Update rsyslog template tests to obtain hostname exclusively from the CONFIG_DB fixture.

#### How to verify it

- Render `rsyslog.conf.j2` with `DEVICE_METADATA.localhost.hostname` set and confirm all SONiC templates use that value.
- Render without hostname metadata and confirm the `sonic` fallback.
- Confirm sanitized hostname values cannot alter rsyslog directives.
